46210209b09507d9148ac04f59da5c5edcea058f: A **Scenario** defines a set of active Roles and a parameterization of the base five-phase interaction protocol (see [RU]protocol-core/index.md §Interaction Protocol) for solving problems of a particular kind. It is a declarative recipe, not an execution instance: a Scenario is what gets selected; a Session is what gets created when a Scenario runs against a Task.[RU]
5f7e3a2a8f116fdbd0cf0883b88ce865cc596832: Scenarios do not replace or extend the core protocol structure. They select roles, tune parameters, and optionally define preparatory pre-phases that feed input into Phase 1 (Task Submission). Protocol-level modifications (different phase sequences, different consensus logic) are handled by separate protocol variants, not by scenarios.[RU]
08d2ce408cc2b4b35e72aade1a186612c239bb81:
| Recipe | **Scenario** | Declares roles, parameters, pre-phases |[RU]
| Input | **Task** | User-submitted problem description |[RU]
| Execution | **Session** | Concrete run combining a Scenario with a Task |[RU]
| Participants | **Roles** | Perspective-driven capacities activated by the Scenario |[RU]
6ef5ad302a09c1c93cea96ffaacb6cabdac88cee: A Scenario selects Roles from the available set defined in [RU]protocol-core. A Scenario parametrizes the base protocol (discussion round limits, subject admission criteria, etc.) but does not alter its phase sequence or consensus logic.[RU]
8247001e091fb52ef78d6e0100b778736c006365: Each Scenario declaration carries the following fields:[RU]
04890a8e29aad77972a20cde8a540302c9206c73:
| name | string | yes | Human-readable identifier |[RU]
| problem_type | string | yes | Free-text description of the problem domain this scenario solves |[RU]
| roles | array of role identifiers | yes | Roles to activate; must include Reliability & Security Specialist unless explicitly excluded with documented operator justification |[RU]
| no_consensus_budget | integer | yes | Maximum number of targeted discussion rounds before a [RU]no-consensus outcome automatically transitions to [RU]blocked-escalation with [RU]escalation_reason = information-gap. Budget counts downward from each round in Phase 3; when it reaches zero, Phase 4 evaluates budget as exhausted rather than [RU]no-consensus. |[RU]
| version | semantic version string | yes | Independent scenario version |[RU]
| scenario_id | string | yes | Stable unique identifier for this scenario definition. REQUIRED — every scenario must provide its own identifier matching the catalog entry. Identifiers are kebab-case and must be globally unique across all scenarios. Inferred from the filename when present in the default catalog ([RU]default-council-session.yaml → [RU]default-council-session). |[RU]
| round_timeout_minutes | integer | no | Default timeout (minutes) for each discussion round. Defaults to [RU]protocol.max_discussion_rounds * 5 when omitted. Used by the runtime to set per-round [RU]timeout_at (see [RU]execution-runtime/index.md §Escalation Routing). |[RU]
| escalation_timeout_minutes | integer | no | Default timeout (minutes) for escalated sessions awaiting operator resolution. Defaults to [RU]defaults/policy.yaml value (30 min) when omitted. Overrides the policy file when present. |[RU]
61bca60abfa1e09eb8a68ebda9c984c92b986456: 1. **Protocol structure immutability.** Scenarios may parameterize the base five-phase protocol but never insert, remove, or reorder phases. The canonical sequence (Task Submission → Individual Review → Discussion Round → Consensus Check → Resolution Formation) is inviolable.[RU]
0d4bc2ba76b7e43d230a99904b2cf7b251488cc9: 2. **Escalation paths preserved.** No scenario may disable or weaken escalation channels (information gap, irresolvable conflict, risk threshold breach).[RU]
a97fe01f1ac2aae7834fbdc8764d31e6d2782ae8: 3. **Consensus computation unchanged.** The deterministic consensus rules (agree/concerns/blocked-in-scope/blocked-escalation evaluation) cannot be overridden by scenario configuration.[RU]
a22e4c3982340d368cf21d5c9363c980bfa763ca: 4. **R&S Specialist inclusion.** The Reliability & Security Specialist role must be present in every scenario by default. Explicit exclusion requires a human-approved reason stored in the session record and a documented justification in Phase 1.[RU]
0508d5e32e87d82444e09c7ac7c1741f4dc44d3b: 5. **Fixed catalog at launch.** Scenarios are authored exclusively by framework maintainers. Operator authoring is deferred until a governance model exists.[RU]
305010b58f7e06db481f573e2a316657dbf9901d: 6. **No composability at MVP.** Scenarios reference other scenarios via a reserved field but cannot compose others at launch. Composition validation semantics will be defined in a later milestone.[RU]

dd4d82734563033577991c0ab8c96c539061294c:
- **Scenario vs Task:** A Task describes *what* needs solving. A Scenario describes *how* the system approaches that type of problem structurally.[RU]
- **Scenario vs Session:** A Scenario is a template/recommendation; a Session is a concrete execution instance with a single Scenario bound to a single Task.[RU]
- **Scenario vs Roles:** A Scenario selects Roles from the available set. It does not redefine them or their responsibilities. Prompt customization within a Scenario is scoped to emphasis/context injection, not behavioral substitution.[RU]
- **Scenario vs Protocol Core:** A Scenario inherits the base five-phase protocol structure from [RU]protocol-core/index.md and parameterizes it. New protocol variants would be separate artifacts referenced independently.[RU]
- **Scenario vs Role Activation Tiers:** The tier model (Core / Extended) in [RU]protocol-core (§Role Activation Rules) serves as the fallback/default mechanism. Scenarios provide declarative overlays that replace manual justification once fully adopted. Until then, tier-based defaults apply when no Scenario is specified.[RU]
cdc765c4814083a7a147f2f032377f4d3115c16a: These scenarios are proposed as illustrative examples. They are NOT part of the initial implementation — the initial implementation consists of documenting the Scenario abstraction itself. Future iterations will populate a curated catalog based on observed usage patterns.[RU]
ec7133e6928590dfb7b59fc0763a1d84a8bbeb2f:
- **Brainstorming** — Multi-perspective ideation session focused on generating options without premature convergence. Likely includes extended discussion rounds.[RU]
- **Grill** — Intense adversarial clarification mode. Multi-round questioning to surface hidden assumptions and requirements before formal review begins. May use higher pre-phase round limits and stricter critical-justification thresholds.[RU]
- **Specification Generation** — Transforms a detailed task description into a structured specification. Minimal pre-phases, possibly zero discussion rounds for well-defined inputs.[RU]
- **Implementation Planning** — Converts a specification into a step-by-step execution plan. Activates Roles that cover architectural decomposition, operational concerns, and sequencing dependencies.[RU]
